artifact-analysis.show: What was made, with what materials, and how it looks and works.
artifact-analysis.limit: How people received or used it, unless you also ask or watch.

automated-remote-research.show: What large numbers of people do in their own settings, at scale.
automated-remote-research.limit: Why they do it, or who they are, beyond what the software records.

behavioral-mapping.show: Where people go and what they do in a space, with counts.
behavioral-mapping.limit: Why they chose a route or activity, or what happens outside the hours you mapped.

buzz-reports.show: What people are saying about a topic right now, and in what words.
buzz-reports.limit: How many people hold a view, or whether their talk matches their behavior.

case-studies.show: How a particular case unfolded in its context, in depth.
case-studies.limit: That other cases would behave the same way.

competitive-testing.show: How competing products compare on the same tasks, using the measures you set.
competitive-testing.limit: Why one product works better, or how any of them perform for people outside your test.

content-inventory-audit.show: What content exists and what condition it is in.
content-inventory-audit.limit: How readers find, use, or understand it.

contextual-inquiry.show: How work really happens in its setting, including workarounds people forget to mention.
contextual-inquiry.limit: Patterns across a wider population, from a few visits.

critical-incident-technique.show: Specific events that helped or hindered, as people recall them.
critical-incident-technique.limit: How often such events happen, or what people forgot.

crowdsourcing.show: A wide range of contributions, quickly, from many people.
crowdsourcing.limit: Who the contributors are, or whether they represent your users.

cultural-probes.show: What participants notice, value, and imagine when given open creative tasks.
cultural-probes.limit: A general claim, since only people who chose to respond are heard.

design-ethnography.show: Meaning, culture, and everyday practice in a setting, built up over time.
design-ethnography.limit: How common a practice is beyond the setting you studied.

diary-studies.show: Experiences and routines over days or weeks, recorded close to when they happened.
diary-studies.limit: What people leave out, or how recording changed what they did.

directed-storytelling.show: One person’s account of a specific experience, in sequence, with emotions and turning points.
directed-storytelling.limit: What the person actually did, or how typical the story is.

ergonomic-analysis.show: Whether a tool or space fits the human body in reach, posture, force, and effort.
ergonomic-analysis.limit: Preferences, meaning, or comfort over long use, unless you also ask.

evidence-based-design.show: What published studies and measured outcomes say about a design choice.
evidence-based-design.limit: Whether those findings hold in your setting or for your users.

experience-sampling-method.show: What people are doing, thinking, or feeling at random moments in daily life.
experience-sampling-method.limit: Why they feel it, or what happens in moments when they could not respond.

experiments.show: Whether a change moves an outcome, and by how much, under controlled conditions.
experiments.limit: Why the effect happens, or whether it holds outside your test.

extremes-and-mainstreams.show: Needs and workarounds at the edges of a population, next to typical use.

fly-on-the-wall-observation.show: Natural behavior, with little influence from you.
fly-on-the-wall-observation.limit: Intentions and reasons, unless you also ask.

focus-groups.show: A range of views and the language a group uses, as people respond to each other.
focus-groups.limit: What individuals would say alone, or what people actually do.

graffiti-walls.show: Quick, candid, anonymous responses to an open prompt.
graffiti-walls.limit: A representative view, since people choose whether to write.

guerilla-user-research.show: Fast first reactions from whoever is available in a public place.
guerilla-user-research.limit: Depth, or the views of people who were not there.

innovation-sourcebook.show: How other organizations solved similar problems, in a comparable form.
innovation-sourcebook.limit: Whether those solutions would work for you.

interviews.show: Experiences, beliefs, attitudes, and stated reasons, in people’s own words.
interviews.limit: What people actually do, or the effect of a change.

laddering.show: The chain from a feature to the personal value behind a preference.
laddering.limit: Whether that chain applies beyond the person you asked.

listening-tour.show: What people in an organization or community raise when they are given the floor.
listening-tour.limit: The views of people who did not take part, or anything the leader’s presence shaped.

literature-reviews.show: What is already known, and where published accounts thin out.
literature-reviews.limit: What is true in your setting, or anything not yet studied.

observation.show: What people do in a real setting, and in what order.
observation.limit: Why they do it, unless you also ask.

participant-observation.show: Practice from the inside, including what people take for granted.
participant-observation.limit: A neutral view, since your participation shapes what you see.

participatory-action-research.show: Change in a setting, shaped by the people affected, and what the group learns by acting.
participatory-action-research.limit: A general claim, or a result that is independent of the people involved.

personal-inventories.show: How a person relates to the objects they own and use.
personal-inventories.limit: How other people relate to similar objects.

photo-studies.show: What participants choose to notice and photograph in their own lives.
photo-studies.limit: Why they chose it, unless you ask about each photo.

picture-cards.show: Associations and feelings that are hard to put into words, through what people choose and explain.
picture-cards.limit: A general claim, since the cards you provide shape the answers.

popular-media-scan.show: How a topic is framed and described in public media.

questionnaires-surveys.show: What many people report about themselves, in a form you can count.
questionnaires-surveys.limit: What people actually do, or why they answered as they did.

remote-moderated-research.show: How people use a product in their own setting, with the chance to ask as they go.
remote-moderated-research.limit: The surroundings you cannot see, or behavior when no one is watching.

secondary-research.show: What published and existing sources already report.
secondary-research.limit: Answers to questions those sources never asked.

semantic-differential.show: How a group rates the feel of a design on named qualities, as numbers.
semantic-differential.limit: Behavior, or why a design feels the way it does.

shadowing.show: A person’s day or task as it unfolds across places and moments.
shadowing.limit: Patterns beyond the person you followed.

site-search-analytics.show: What people search for and where searches fail.
site-search-analytics.limit: Why they searched, or what they wanted when they typed nothing.

the-love-letter-the-breakup-letter.show: Strong feelings about a product, in the writer’s own words.
the-love-letter-the-breakup-letter.limit: Everyday use, or the views of people who did not write.

touchstone-tours.show: How a person relates to a space and its objects, as they narrate a walk through it.
touchstone-tours.limit: How other people experience the same space.

triading.show: The distinctions people draw between items, in their own words.

unobtrusive-measures.show: Traces of behavior left behind, such as wear, litter, or logs, with no contact with participants.
unobtrusive-measures.limit: Who left the traces, or why.

abstraction-laddering.show: A problem reframed at higher and lower levels of purpose.
abstraction-laddering.limit: Whether the reframing is right. It stays your interpretation until you test it.

aeiou.show: Field notes sorted into activities, environments, interactions, objects, and users.
aeiou.limit: The reasons for behavior, unless you also ask.

affinity-diagramming.show: Themes that recur across notes, quotes, and observations.
affinity-diagramming.limit: Anything the data did not already contain, or how common a theme is.

bulls-eye-diagramming.show: Which findings a group ranks as most important, in agreed rings.
bulls-eye-diagramming.limit: Why they matter. The ranking reflects the people who ranked.

card-sorting.show: How people group and name items, and which categories make sense to them.
card-sorting.limit: Whether a structure works when people use it.

cognitive-mapping.show: How a person connects ideas about a topic, drawn as a map.
cognitive-mapping.limit: Whether other people think the same way.

concept-mapping.show: How ideas relate to each other around a central topic.
concept-mapping.limit: Whether the relationships hold beyond the person who drew the map.

content-analysis.show: Patterns in text, media, or images, counted against a coding scheme.

create-insight-statements.show: Findings stated as a tension worth designing for.
create-insight-statements.limit: That the insight is true. It is an interpretation of your data.

elito-method.show: A traceable path from observation to interpretation to design consequence.

eraf-systems-diagram.show: The entities, relationships, and flows in a system.
eraf-systems-diagram.limit: How the system behaves over time.

experience-diagramming.show: A user’s steps, thoughts, and feelings across an experience.
experience-diagramming.limit: The experiences of people you did not study.

find-themes.show: Recurring patterns in the data, named as topics.
find-themes.limit: How many people share each theme.

importancedifficulty-matrix.show: Items sorted by value against effort.
importancedifficulty-matrix.limit: Whether the estimates of value and effort are right.

kano-analysis.show: Which features people expect, want, or do not care about.
kano-analysis.limit: Behavior, or what people would pay for.

kj-technique.show: Groups that appear when a team clusters notes in silence.
kj-technique.limit: Anything beyond the notes the team brought.

mental-model-diagrams.show: How people think and act around a task, set against what a product offers.
mental-model-diagrams.limit: A model that holds for everyone.

mind-mapping.show: Related ideas branching from one topic.
mind-mapping.limit: Which ideas are good or true.

personas.show: Patterns of behavior and need, described as a typical person.
personas.limit: Real individuals, or how many people fit each persona.

poems.show: Observations sorted into people, objects, environments, messages, and services.
poems.limit: The reasons for behavior, unless you also ask.

problem-tree-analysis.show: Proposed causes and consequences of a core problem.
problem-tree-analysis.limit: That the causes are real. They are hypotheses until checked.

rose-thorn-bud.show: What a team sees as working, painful, or promising.

stakeholder-maps.show: Who has an interest in a system and how they relate to each other.
stakeholder-maps.limit: What each stakeholder will actually do.

statement-starters.show: Problems reframed as open questions that invite ideas.
statement-starters.limit: Whether the question is the right one.

symmetric-clustering-matrix.show: Which items relate most strongly when each is scored against the others.

task-analysis.show: The actions, decisions, and system responses that make up a task.
task-analysis.limit: Why people depart from the steps.

ten-types-of-innovation-diagnostics.show: Where an organization’s offerings are strong or thin across ten types of innovation.

territory-maps.show: How a large body of research findings clusters into areas.
territory-maps.limit: Which areas matter most to users.

thematic-networks.show: How basic themes build into larger themes in text data.
thematic-networks.limit: Anything beyond the text you coded.

top-five.show: The findings or ideas a team finds most compelling.
top-five.limit: That the team’s choices match what users need.

visualize-the-vote.show: Where a group’s attention and preferences lie.
visualize-the-vote.limit: Whether the preferred option is the better one.

word-clouds.show: Which words appear most often in a body of text.
word-clouds.limit: What those words mean in context.

alternative-worlds.show: Ideas borrowed from how another context solves a similar problem.
alternative-worlds.limit: Whether those ideas transfer to yours.

analogous-inspiration.show: Ideas drawn from an unrelated setting that shares a pattern with your problem.
analogous-inspiration.limit: Whether the pattern really carries over.

bodystorming.show: Ideas that come from acting out a situation in a space.
bodystorming.limit: Whether the ideas work for real users.

brainstorm-graphic-organizers.show: A structured spread of ideas around a topic.
brainstorm-graphic-organizers.limit: Which ideas are feasible or wanted.

brainstorming.show: A large number of ideas in a short time.
brainstorming.limit: Which ideas are good, feasible, or wanted.

bundle-ideas.show: Stronger concepts built by combining related ideas.
bundle-ideas.limit: Whether a bundle appeals to users.

co-creation-session.show: What users make and say when they help generate ideas.
co-creation-session.limit: A general claim, since a few participants shaped the ideas.

concept-metaphors-and-analogies.show: New angles on a concept from comparing it to something familiar.

concept-generating-matrix.show: Ideas generated in each combination of two sets of categories.

creative-toolkits.show: What participants build or draw to express what they want.
creative-toolkits.limit: A general claim, since the kit shapes what people make.

design-charette.show: Many ideas and critiques produced quickly by designers and stakeholders together.
design-charette.limit: How the ideas perform with users.

design-workshops.show: Ideas and agreements produced by a group in a structured session.
design-workshops.limit: Whether they hold up outside the room.

draw-it.show: Visual ideas that words would not produce.
draw-it.limit: Whether the sketches are feasible or wanted.

ideation-game.show: Ideas prompted by the structure of a game.

image-boards.show: A mood or direction, expressed through images.
image-boards.limit: What users make of that direction.

mash-ups.show: New concepts made by combining qualities from different things.
mash-ups.limit: Whether a mash-up works in use.

morphological-synthesis.show: Solution combinations built systematically from parts.

round-robin.show: Ideas that build on each other as they pass between people.

thumbnail-sketching.limit: How they work, or whether people want them.

ab-testing.show: Which of two versions performs better on a measured outcome with real users.
ab-testing.limit: Why one version wins, or what to try next.

appearance-modeling.show: How a design will look and feel in a realistic model.
appearance-modeling.limit: Whether it works, or whether people want it.

behavioral-prototype.show: How people behave with a concept before a physical prototype exists.
behavioral-prototype.limit: How the finished product would perform.

business-model-canvas.show: How the parts of a business model fit together on one page.
business-model-canvas.limit: Whether customers will pay, or whether the model will work.

business-origami.show: How a system or service works, simulated with paper figures.
business-origami.limit: How it would run at scale.

cognitive-walkthrough.show: Where a first-time user is likely to get stuck in a task, as judged by experts.

desirability-testing.show: Which words people choose to describe a design, positive and negative.

experience-prototyping.show: How people respond to a concept in a simulated physical or social setting.
experience-prototyping.limit: How they respond in real life.

heuristic-evaluation.show: Likely usability problems, found by experts against a set of principles.
heuristic-evaluation.limit: Which problems real users face, or how severe those problems are for them.

live-prototyping.show: How a concept performs in a real setting with real people.
live-prototyping.limit: Why people respond as they do, unless you also ask.

paper-prototyping.show: Whether the structure and flow of an interface make sense, early and cheaply.
paper-prototyping.limit: How it looks, feels, or performs in a finished form.

parallel-prototyping.show: How different directions compare before a team commits to one.
parallel-prototyping.limit: Which direction will succeed in the world.

rapid-iterative-testing-evaluation.show: Whether fixes made after one round of testing solved the problems found.
rapid-iterative-testing-evaluation.limit: Whether the results hold with a larger group.

role-playing.show: Where a service experience is frustrating, acted out by people.

scenario-description-swimlanes.show: Who does what, and when, in a scenario.
scenario-description-swimlanes.limit: Whether the scenario happens as described.

stakeholder-walkthrough.show: How stakeholders read the findings, and what they add.
stakeholder-walkthrough.limit: Whether their reading matches users’ experience.

storyboarding.show: How an experience unfolds over time, drawn as a sequence.
storyboarding.limit: How people would actually experience it.

think-aloud-protocol.show: What people are thinking as they use a design.
think-aloud-protocol.limit: Thoughts people cannot or do not say aloud, or their natural pace of use.

usability-report.show: A summary of what usability testing found and what to fix.
usability-report.limit: More than the tests it reports on.

usability-testing.show: Where people struggle to complete tasks with a design.
usability-testing.limit: Why they would choose it over others, or how they use it over time.

wizard-of-oz.show: How people respond to a system’s behavior before it is built.
wizard-of-oz.limit: Whether it can be built, or how it would perform at scale.
